newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alfa sees healthy 1996 earnings results.
newsitem.headline: Alfa sees healthy 1996 earnings results.

text.p: Mexican industrial giant Alfa obtained "very good" earnings results during 1996, company CEO Dionisio Garza Medina said on Wednesday.
"The numbers are very good ... because in our units other than petrochemicals and steel we did significantly better," Garza Medina told reporters.
The Monterrey-based Alfa has divisions in petrochemicals, steel, food, telecommunications and retail.

"The decline in business we saw in Petrotemex and in flat steel was more than made up for by the rest of our operations," Garza Medina said. Petrotemex is one of Alfa's main petrochemical subsidiaries and has been hit by lower prices for some of its products.
Garza Medina said Alfa is interested in exploring new possibilities in telecommunications through its stake in Alestra, a venture with AT&T and Mexican holding company VISA-Bancomer.

"We are looking at projects in (personal communications systems) and fixed wireless. These are projects that after the auctions of the radio spectrum this year we will look very seriously at," he said.

Personal communications systems is considered the next generations of cellular technology and has capacity for digital voice and data transmission. ((-- Daniel Perez Whitaker, Monterrey bureau +528 345-7677))
